pairs.subject: delivery-guarantees
pairs.evidence: packages/kernel/src/job-worker.ts:75 Recovery runs before the worker loop but not periodically within it, so a subsequently crashed worker's running jobs can continue occupying capacity until another recovery runs.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/job.ts:108 BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes the claim's state check and update, and later writes check the lease fence; nevertheless, the claim uses an update by identity rather than the standard's explicitly required single conditional pending-to-processing write.
packages/kernel/src/effects.ts:8 Vendor-job effects cross the queue store boundary; job-run performs the asynchronous step between separate dispatch and booking transactions.

packages/kernel/src/job.ts:314 Failed and interrupted jobs remain visible and support individual operator retry, but the inspected job APIs and Runs surface lack the required bulk redrive/discard workflow with per-item outcomes and an explicit dead-letter retention policy.

packages/kernel/src/job-core.ts:90 The producer contract supplies stable identity and documents interruption risk, but leaves vendor deduplication optional and does not name a delivery posture per producer class with the required duplicate-effect analysis.

packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts:331 A step output is recorded only after perform returns a validated produced outcome, within the fenced booking transaction; dispatch records the separate in-flight stage beforehand.
packages/kernel/src/job.ts:307 Cancellation durably records the actor and transition, but accepts and writes no closed-vocabulary non-delivery reason or explicit replayability classification.

packages/domain/src/lane.ts:8 These lanes group resource capacity rather than conversation or document streams; upstream-dependent jobs remain planned until released, while paid-lane crash holds address uncertain spend.

packages/kernel/src/job-core.ts:289 Successful steps reset the failure streak, and attempt increments only on operator retry; the bounded consecutive-failure breaker does not provide the standard's persisted per-item attempt budget across partial progress.

packages/kernel/src/job-queue-core.ts:77 The worker counts running records against capacity without periodically recovering expired claims, so a full lane containing dead workers' jobs cannot reach claim-triggered recovery; startup recovery alone misses this case.

pairs.registryProposal: Clarify whether atomic-claiming intentionally excludes SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions that serialize state checks and writes; the current text explicitly requires a single conditional update and rejects a lock around the read/write pair.
